name: Emerald K9
tagline: Calm hands. Happy dogs. Real trust.
brandNarrative:
Emerald K9 isn't your average grooming salon — it's a one-on-one sanctuary where anxious, shy, and sensitive dogs finally feel safe. Groomer Kaley has built something rare in Portland: a calm, unhurried space where dogs like Vinny the mini Goldendoodle, Joey the rescued chihuahua, and Magic the black Pomeranian have gone from dreading the grooming table to genuinely looking forward to their visits. Customers don't just praise the results — they talk about transformation, trust, and the kind of patience that turns a fearful dog into a confident one.

What sets Emerald K9 apart is Kaley's philosophy: slow down, read the dog, and never rush the process. She started working with Vinny at just four months old, training him for grooming from the very beginning. She worked gradually with Joey, a mature rescue with anxious behavior, until the dog's personality blossomed. She somehow made Magic — a dog who used to come home upset — practically lose his fear of grooming entirely. These aren't flukes. This is method. Clients describe Kaley as patient, gentle, warm, and deeply kind — someone whose love for dogs is palpable in every interaction.

Based in the Pearl District at 1720 NW Lovejoy, Emerald K9 holds a near-perfect 4.9-star rating across 37 reviews. The studio atmosphere — cozy, personal, never chaotic — is by design. Kaley keeps the environment calm and distraction-free so every dog gets her full attention. Whether she's sculpting a dapper cut on an anxious rescue or perfecting the styling on a competition-worthy poodle, the result is always the same: dogs that leave looking impeccable and owners who leave feeling deeply grateful.
ownerStory:
Kaley is the heart and hands behind Emerald K9 — and if you read even a handful of reviews, her name comes up again and again, not as a service provider but as someone clients genuinely trust with the animals they love most. She didn't set out to run just another grooming shop. She built a studio rooted in the belief that grooming should never be a stressful experience for a dog, and that the right approach — calm, patient, one-on-one — can genuinely change an animal's relationship with the process entirely. From training puppies for their very first groom to rehabilitating rescue dogs with deep anxiety, Kaley's work goes well beyond scissors and shampoo.

Her clients describe a warmth and attentiveness that's hard to fake and impossible to mass-produce. She remembers each dog's quirks, adjusts her approach to their needs, and sends them home not just looking great but feeling good about what just happened. The friendship she built with Vinny, the trust she earned from Joey, the transformation she sparked in Magic — these are the stories that define Emerald K9. For Kaley, grooming is care. And in Portland's Pearl District, word has gotten out.

faq.question: My dog is really anxious about grooming. Can Kaley still help?
faq.answer: Absolutely — anxious and fearful dogs are actually something Kaley specializes in. Multiple clients have brought in rescue dogs or pets with severe grooming anxiety and seen dramatic improvements over time. Kaley takes a slow, patient, one-on-one approach that builds genuine trust with each dog at their own pace.

faq.question: Do you work with puppies who have never been groomed before?
faq.answer: Yes, and starting early is actually ideal. Kaley worked with Vinny the mini Goldendoodle from just 4 months old, training him to be comfortable with the grooming process from the very beginning. Early introduction sessions help puppies build positive associations that last a lifetime.

faq.question: What makes Emerald K9 different from a typical grooming salon?
faq.answer: Emerald K9 is a private, one-on-one studio — not a high-volume shop. Kaley sees one dog at a time, which keeps the environment calm and free from the noise and chaos that can stress dogs out. Clients consistently describe it as a completely different experience from traditional groomers.

faq.question: How often should I bring my dog in for grooming?
faq.answer: It depends on your dog's breed, coat type, and lifestyle, but most clients with doodles, poodles, and similar breeds visit every 6–8 weeks to maintain their cut and coat health. Kaley can recommend a schedule based on your specific dog during your first appointment.

faq.question: What breeds does Kaley work with?
faq.answer: Kaley has experience with a wide range of breeds — reviews mention Goldendoodles, Chihuahuas, Pomeranians, French Bulldogs, Scottish Terriers, and Poodles. Whether your dog is a small anxious rescue or a fluffy doodle in need of a precision cut, Emerald K9 has you covered.

faq.question: How do I book an appointment?
faq.answer: The best way to reach Emerald K9 is by phone at (971) 413-5772. The studio is located at 1720 NW Lovejoy St, Suite 112 in Portland's Pearl District. Since it's a private one-on-one studio, availability can fill up — reaching out early is recommended.

brandColors.note: Deep emerald green anchors the brand name and evokes calm, nature, and trustworthiness — exactly what anxious dog owners need to feel. The soft mint accent keeps the palette approachable and gentle rather than corporate, matching Kaley's warm, personal grooming style.
